items.text: Weekly KYC backlog: 140 open cases as of this morning, up from 112 last Monday. Biggest bottleneck by far is SanctionsScreen latency, with screening calls regularly taking 40-60s and some timing out, so cases sit in pending-screen and analysts re-run them by hand. @Sam Okafor @Omar Brown can IT take a look this week and get us a fix or at least a workaround? Happy to share the slow-case export.

items.title: KYCPipeline: DocVault upload timeouts blocking onboarding
items.text:
Since roughly Monday, KYCPipeline document uploads to DocVault are timing out intermittently during the onboarding step. The pipeline waits on the DocVault write, hits the current 30s timeout, and the case drops into an error state with no automatic retry. Analysts then have to re-upload manually or work around it.

Example case: client {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0010}} has been stuck since Tuesday because their ID scan failed to upload (three attempts, all timed out). To keep the file moving, the KYC team verified SSN {{CLIENT_SSN:c_0010}} and date of birth {{CLIENT_DOB:c_0010}} manually against the source documents. The case still can't clear CDD until the scan is attached in DocVault.

Impact: about 18 cases are affected so far. Lending flagged two LoanOrigination files waiting on KYC clearance as a result.

Ask: Technology please review DocVault upload latency and the KYCPipeline client timeout setting. Larger scans (multi-page PDFs over 8MB) seem to fail most often.

--- Comment by Leo Martinez ---
Looked at DocVault logs. Upload p95 for files over 5MB is around 34s since Monday's storage tier change, so the KYCPipeline client's 30s timeout is too tight. We're raising the client timeout to 120s and the DocVault ingress timeout to match. Change goes out in tonight's window.

--- Comment by Omar Brown ---
Timeout change deployed at 21:40 ET. No upload timeouts in the last 12 hours, and p95 upload is now about 36s with no failures. We'll track the storage tier latency separately.

--- Comment by Ravi Patel ---
Confirmed on our side. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0010}}'s ID scan uploaded on the first try this morning and the case cleared CDD. The other 17 stuck cases were reprocessed successfully. Separately, we'd like proper retry logic in the pipeline at some point, but resolving this one. Thanks Leo and Omar.

items.title: KYCPipeline ownership moving to Compliance Engineering
items.text:
Hi Ravi and Jenna,

I want to confirm the plan we discussed with Marcus last week. Ownership of KYCPipeline will move from Operations (Ravi) to Compliance Engineering (Jenna), effective Tuesday, October 6, 2026. The pipeline is so closely tied to SanctionsScreen and our CDD policy that it makes sense for Compliance Engineering to own it end to end, including the roadmap, on-call and vendor relationships.

Ravi, thank you for running this through a heavy year. You'll stay on as the escalation contact through the end of October so Jenna's team has a backstop while they settle in.

To make the transition clean, please put together a handover checklist together. At minimum it should cover:
- open tickets and known issues (SanctionsScreen latency, DocVault retry behavior after KYC-045)
- runbooks, alert routing and on-call rotation
- access and entitlements
- current backlog status and SLA reporting

Please send me a draft by September 29.

Thanks,
Linda

Quick org note: as of today, KYCPipeline is owned by Jenna Cho's Compliance Engineering team. Please route pipeline questions and issues to Jenna's team in #kyc-pipeline. Huge thanks to Ravi Patel and the Operations team for running it and for a very thorough handover 🙏

First update from Compliance Engineering as the new KYCPipeline owner 👋 Our top priorities are (1) SanctionsScreen latency, which is still the biggest driver of the backlog, and (2) proper retries for DocVault uploads so we don't have a repeat of KYC-045. I'll hold office hours Thursdays 2-3pm ET for anyone onboarding or lending who wants to bring stuck cases or questions. Ravi stays our escalation backstop through the end of October.
